recipes.name: Butternut Squash Soup with a Kick
ingredients_raw: 1 (2 pound) butternut squash - peeled, seeded, and cubed
salt and black pepper to taste
1 tablespoon chopped fresh thyme, or to taste

steps.text: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion, jalapeño, and ginger; cook and stir until onion has softened and turned translucent, about 7 minutes.
Add butternut squash and chicken broth; bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until squash is tender, about 30 minutes.
Stir in evaporated milk, coconut milk, sugar, salt, and black pepper; cook and stir 5 minutes more.

Fill a blender halfway with soup. Cover and hold lid down with a folded kitchen towel; pulse a few times before leaving on to purée. Pour into a clean pot. Repeat with remaining soup. Or purée soup with an immersion blender until smooth. Garnish servings with sour cream and thyme.

raw_recipe.headline: Butternut Squash Soup with a Kick
raw_recipe.description: Fresh ginger and jalapeño pepper spice up this silky butternut squash soup with a kick recipe. Sour cream and fresh thyme cool it down to your liking.

review.reviewBody: Yum!!! I prefer the squash roasted. Split the squash in half, salt & pepper and put 1 TB butter in before roasting 1 1/2 hours. Pour the juices out into soup pot before cutting so you don't lose the liquid. It was great as it was, but the heat was minimal. I will make again with more jalapeno so I can try it with sour cream. Thank you so much for the recipe!

Perfect! I added garlic. I also did not have coconut milk, so I added unsweetened grated coconut prior to blending. I also added heavy cream at the end in the place of coconut milk. This was a family favorite. The spicy jalapeno is a perfect complement.

This was amazing!!! I only changed a couple things. First off, I didn't use a chicken broth, I had chicken bouillon from epicure that I made into a broth. I made a little extra because I didn't have condensed milk. Instead I used a whole can of coconut cream instead of a half a cup of coconut milk. I also roasted the squash in olive oil for about 30-40 minutes already cubed up and at 350*. My last alteration was because I didn't have a jalapeños, I used some hot peppers from our garden. With the way everything cooked down, I didn't even need to purée. I whisked it while it simmered and we love having little bites of garlic/onion/pepper pieces in our soups. Everything was chopped so fine anyway so I don't think you need to Purée it unless you want to make it completely smooth. It was very smooth even by just whisking it. Very excited to have leftovers at lunch tomorrow! And you can toast the seeds in the oven at 250* for about 30-40 minutes (until crispy) or so with olive oil and salt (and pepper)... Just as yummy as pumpkin seeds! So glad I did it!

Beyond delicious. Halved the squash, and roasted with a dab of butter and salt/pepper at 375 degrees for 1-1/4 hours. Threw in 1/2 red bell pepper and a large carrot since needing to use up. Didn’t de-seed the jalapeno as we wanted the soup to have some kick (davey’s personal recipe only dices the jalapeno so seeding it is likely an AR edit; probably why a number of reviewers think it lacks heat). Omitted the sugar. Added several splashes of sauvignon blanc, 1 teaspoon curry, and 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg. Will double this recipe the next time. Thanks, davey, for sharing a superb recipe.

Best soup ever! My family was skeptical but they all went back for seconds! I did alter it a little. I used one 4oz can of chopped and peeled green chiles instead of jalapeño, I baked 2 butternut squash instead of peeling and cubing it (cut in half, remove seeds, face down on cookie sheet for 45-60 mins at 350 degrees), and used 2 cans of chicken broth. I did not use ginger as my family doesn't like it. After tasting it, I didn't use sour cream or thyme. It was awesome as is!

I’ve been making a slightly healthier variation of this recipe for years! Because butternut squash is often very difficult to cut and takes a long time to cook I usually splurge a little and buy a 24oz clamshell of cubed butternut squash at the grocery. That way, I can make this in under 30 minutes I use EVOO rather than butter, add minced garlic (about 4 cloves) to the sautée, and use light coconut milk, no evaporated, Also, brown sugar instead of white, and garnish with low or fat-free plain Greek yogurt before eating. It’s great hot and it’s also wonderful as a cold soup in the summer!

Great starting point. Left out the (bizarre) coconut and evaporated milk and used 1 c regular milk instead. Jalapeno seems an odd choice with butternut squash, so I substituted 1/2 tsp crushed red pepper, and 1/4 tsp each turmeric and paprika. Cooked the onions longer than called for too, and added the thyme to the sauteed onions. The resulting soup had a nice earthy spicy flavor, without the bite of jalapeño.

I followed the recipe almost to the letter, except I added 1tsp of curry and I used 1tsp cayenne powder because I didn't have a fresh jalapeno. I didn't puree it, as I rather liked the chunkier texture. This and some crusty french bread will make for a stick to your insides comfort dinner on a blustery, winter night. Loved the flavor and the texture!

This is my go to recipe and have been using for yrs! Always satisfies! Always Delish! Have shared this recipe with family & friends who absolutely love as well. Over the years because of health reasons I changed a few things but, this is still delish. Like others, I always roast the squash. Leave whole, prick a few holes with a fork. Place on parchment paper and roast at 400° for 50-70 mins. Let cool, slice open, remove seeds, and scoop out the squash. I also, made the following substitutions: 2 Tablespoons of Regular Sesame Oil (not toasted) for butter, 1 Tablespoon of 100% Maple Syrup or Maple Sugar instead of white sugar, and I add 1-2 teaspoons of ground Tumeric. Serve with Pepitas or Roasted Pumpkin Seeds. I omit the sour cream & thyme. Everything else remains the same.

Delicious! Halved the squash, cleaned out the seeds, put 2 tsp butter in the pitted out area of both halves. Sprinkled with paprika, thyme, cayenne, and ginger to taste. Roasted the butternut squash on 375 deg F for 75 min. After the butter melted, used a grill brush to coat squash with the butter. Diced the onion but also added a diced red bell pepper and used 2 jalapeños. Sautéed with a tsp of butter and added half the can of chicken broth. Once cooked thoroughly, added the butternut squash and remainder of the chicken broth along with the evaporated milk and coconut milk. Brought to a boil and added salt and pepper to taste. Puréed in the blender then added back to a clean pot and simmered on low for another 30 min. Served with sprinkled paprika and thyme as well as a "dollop of daisy".

It was the best soup I've ever eaten. The modifications I made...
- Cut and cubed butternut, coated w coconut oil and roasted at 350 degrees. 
- I had no evaporated milk but google says a good substitution is 3/4 water mixed with 2/3 powdered milk to equal 1 cup evaporated milk. They're the same thing! 
- I added an extra jalapeño pepper to sauté. I used coconut oil to sauté instead of butter.
- I added paprika powder and turmeric powder after the milk and coconut milk was poured in and mixed along with sea salt and pepper. I let it cook a little longer to allow flavors to meld then puree. 
- No need for sour cream! 
- For a diary-free soup - it is totally ok to increase the coconut milk and eliminate the evaporated milk. It'll still taste delicious!
Easy to put together but its very bland.
My FAV squash soup recipe! I get multiple requests for it every time. I put a lil extra ginger and jalapeño. 😋

I combined a couple recipes and also added some of my own ideas. I had some pureed winter squash in my freezer that I had cooked in my Instant Pot. I had stored them in ziplocks. It must have been at least a decent size butter nut. I set the ziplocks in warm water while I chopped veggies. I diced up several carrots, and onion and fried them in avocado oil on medium heat until tender. I then added my (half thawed squash) and put it on low heat. Later I added 1 can of evaporated milk, several dishes of cumin, several dashes of thyme, 10 twists of black pepper from a pepper mill, several dashes of smoked paprika (from Wally world), 2 diced Granny Smith apples with the peels on, a few dashes of some green hot sauce I had left over in my fridge, and about 10 shakes of cayenne pepper powder, and a squirt of some garlic I bought from Aldi. I like it spicy! I simmered this another 15 minutes. It was very thick like chunky apple sauce. It was delicious and once it cools down a bit I will blend it into a puree. I thought about adding a cream cheese into it too.

I’ve made this soup as written many times and it never disappoints. It is my husband’s favourite. Sometimes I add curry powder and garam marsala as well. Just takes it up a notch. The hardest part is peeling the squash.
Very tasty. Used 12 slices of picked pepper and roasted squash. Too spicy. Next time will reduce it to 4-6 slices. Will try using the coconut cream from the top of the can to sauté the onions.
Beyond delicious !
This is the BEST butternut squash recipe I have ever found. I love it! I used habanero pepper because that is what I had from garden, and it was perfect.

I've been making this for years but now do a vegan version- olive oil instead of butter, vegetable stock instead of chicken, and all coconut milk rather than evaporated. I actually prefer the vegan version! I also prefer leeks to onions. So, so good and easy to play with as the description suggests.

Added 1 tsp. Hot sauce instead of peppers. Added 2 tsp curry 
Garnished with grated cheese, green onions & croutons.
